title: The Leech Cure
text: A marsh doctor in a coat of eel skin offers to bleed your wounded with his prize leeches, which he keeps fat, black and writhing in a jar. He swears by them. He has a great many grateful patients, he says, though none of them are here.

options.label: Let him bleed the wounded with his prize leeches.

outcomes.text: The wounded come away pale but mending, dotted with little round scars.
These are not his prize leeches, and they leave something behind.

options.label: The sharpest asks to see his notes before anyone bares an arm.

outcomes.text: The notes are mostly gibberish, but one recipe in them is sound.

options.label: Refuse his leeches politely; you have bled enough.

outcomes.text: He sulks into the reeds. His leeches do not: at dusk you find them on your legs, fat and sleepy.
